sections.heading: We Put an Owner on Your Roof
body: Most roofing companies send a commissioned salesperson. Plenty never climb a ladder, and many price your roof straight off the insurance paperwork.
A person paid by the sale has a reason to find you a new roof. We have no commissioned salespeople and no project managers, so nobody here earns more if the answer is "replace."

Doug started this company, and his son Jason handles most of what you'll see: the call, the inspection, the quote and the insurance. You can always speak with an owner, and most of the time it's Jason who climbs up and looks at your roof himself.
Owner on the roof. Scope, warranty and price in writing. That's the whole method.

sections.heading: What We Find When We Get Up There
body: Most roof calls start with something you see on the ceiling or in the yard. Here is what usually causes it, and what we do about it.

items.title: A brown stain on the ceiling under a tile roof that looks fine
items.text: Tile sheds water, but the underlayment beneath it is what keeps the house dry, and it wears out long before the tile does. If the underlayment has failed, we lift the tile, put down new underlayment and lay your same tile back.

items.title: Cracked or slipped tiles after hail or wind
items.text: A broken tile lets water reach the underlayment, and a near-match replacement looks like a patch and may not seal like the original. We order tile that matches, and Jason takes it up with your insurer when a storm did the damage.

items.title: A leak that came back after someone else fixed it
items.text: The last repair probably patched the spot above the stain, while the water got in several feet uphill and ran along the deck. We check the whole roof, find where the water really enters and fix that.

items.title: Water around a chimney, skylight or sky tube
items.text: Flashing is thin metal shaped to that exact spot, and it loosens with age or gets smeared with caulk. We rework the flashing instead of sealing over it.

items.title: Shingles in the yard after a wind storm
items.text: Wind gets under shingles whose sealant strip never bonded or has aged out, and once a tab lifts, the next gust tears it off. We replace what's missing and check the rest for creased tabs and hail bruising.

items.title: Cedar shakes split, curled or missing
items.text: Wood shake dries, splits and rots, and a loose shake lets water straight through. Very few roofers have the skill to repair wood shake, and we do.

tail: A working Wichita roofer sent the homeowner below to us for his tile repair.

Jason recognized the botched repair and corrected it before it had a chance to damage the inside of the house.  It pays to have it done-right the first time.

sections.heading: Tile Is Our Specialty, and Matching It Matters
body: Concrete and clay tile come in different shapes, profiles and colors, and a tile that has weathered for twenty years never matches a new one. A near match looks like a patch, and if the profile is off, it doesn't seal like the original.
So we order matching tile. We've worked on everything from concrete barrel tile to Ludowici tile on a National Register home.

items.q: Can my roof be repaired, or do I need a new one?
items.a: It depends on how far the damage spreads. A leak at one valley, one flashing or one patch of underlayment is a repair. Broken tile or bruised shingles across most of the roof, or leaks showing up in more than one room, point to replacement. From the ground, look for granules piling up at the downspouts and cracked tile in more than one area.

items.q: Do you work with insurance companies?
items.a: Yes. Jason works with your insurer from the first call to the finished roof. We price from what's on your roof, not just from the paperwork, and we'll tell you if the claim covers less than the roof needs.

Every repair and re-roof estimate is written and lists the scope of work, the warranty and the price. Set it beside any other bid and check underlayment, flashing, ridge and hip, decking and cleanup item by item.

Workmanship warranties run from 5 to 15 years, depending on the roof and the job, and products that carry lifetime manufacturer warranties come with them. The term for your job is written on your estimate.

sections.heading: Replace It or Repair It?
body: A leak at one valley or one flashing is a [roof repair](/roof-repair-wichita-ks/), and we'd rather fix that than sell you a roof. We have no commissioned salespeople, so nobody here earns more if your answer is "replace."

Replacement makes sense when the damage is spread across the roof. Hail or wind has broken or bruised the surface in many places, the shingles are curling and shedding granules everywhere, or the same roof keeps leaking in new spots.
At that point every repair costs you money without ending the problem.

sections.heading: Start With the Material
body: Most roofers quote one product, the one they sell all day. We install five kinds of roof, so we can tell you which one fits your house instead of which one fits our truck.
Here is how they differ, in plain terms.

items.title: Concrete and clay tile
items.text: Heavy, fireproof and long-lived, and the look that suits a lot of older Wichita homes. The tile outlasts everything under it, so a good tile roof is as much about the underlayment as the tile.

items.title: DaVinci
items.text: Molded composite that looks like slate or cedar shake, without the upkeep. We were one of the first roofers in the Wichita area to install it, as early as 2002, so we've seen how it holds up through a lot of Kansas weather.

items.title: Brava
items.text: Synthetic tile, shake and slate that reads as the real material from the street. It's a good answer when you love the look of cedar shake but don't want to re-treat and replace split shakes.

items.title: Premium asphalt
items.text: Atlas StormMaster Shake and CertainTeed Presidential Shake are thick, dimensional shingles cut to throw the shadow lines of shake, and we recommend Atlas. Some premium lines carry a Class 4 impact rating and a manufacturer's wind warranty up to 130 mph, so in hail country, check those on the exact product you're pricing.

items.title: Standing seam metal
items.text: The fasteners hide under the raised seams, so there are no exposed screws to work loose and leak. We typically use the horizon lock panel from Central States Manufacturing.

sections.heading: What a Replacement Involves
body: The old roofing comes off, and any decking that's soft or rotted gets replaced before new material goes on. New underlayment and flashing go down, then the roof itself.

A shingle roof often takes a day or two. Tile takes longer, because it is heavy, comes off by hand and goes on the same way. The crew cleans up each day, so you are not living in a debris field for the length of the job.

Weather sets the schedule too. Asphalt shingles have a strip of sealant that bonds in the warmth; laid on a cold day, they can sit unsealed and lift in the next wind. So we watch the temperature, not just the calendar.

sections.heading: Leaks Traced to the Real Cause
body: Most roof repairs fail for one reason: someone patched the spot above the stain. The leak comes back with the next rain, and now there's tar on the roof and a second repair bill.
We start by looking at the whole roof, not just the stain. We check the flashing, the valleys, the penetrations and the surface, and we tell you what we found before we fix anything.

Sometimes the answer is a small repair. Sometimes it is the first sign of something bigger, and we'll say so. If the roof is past fixing, we'll tell you that too, and show you what a [roof replacement](/roof-replacement-wichita-ks/) would involve.

sections.heading: Tile Roof Repair
body: Concrete and clay tile are tough, and they still leak. The tile isn't the weak point. The underlayment beneath it, the valleys and the flashing are.

For a cracked or broken tile, we replace it with a tile that matches. For a failed valley or flashing, we rebuild that detail. For a worn-out underlayment, we lift the tile in the affected area, put down new underlayment and relay the same tile.
That lift-and-relay work is slow and takes a crew that has done it many times, because tile that's walked on wrong cracks. It's also what keeps an old tile roof out of the dumpster.

sections.quote: Removed every piece of our roof clay tile, discarded the old underlayment with a new improved product and then returned the existing clay tile. Very labor intensive and time consuming. The crew of four did everything stated and were wonderful to work with.

sections.heading: Valleys, Flashing and Sky Tubes
body: Water goes where a roof changes direction or where something pokes through it. That makes valleys, chimney flashing, skylights and sky tubes the usual suspects.

Flashing is thin metal that has to be shaped and sealed to that exact spot. It ages, loosens and gets sealed with caulk by whoever came before. We rework flashing from eave to rake, around chimneys and around skylights, and replace what has worn out instead of smearing over it.
Valleys carry the most water on the roof, so they wear first. A worn valley is a repair worth doing before it becomes a ceiling.

sections.quote: This past year they replaced the outside of my sky tubes that were leaking and repaired the valleys that were deteriorating, using a new type of product that should keep them worry free for years.

sections.heading: Wood Shake and Shingle Repair
body: Cedar shakes split, curl and rot, and a loose one lets water straight through. Very few roofing companies have the skill to repair wood shake and wood shingles, and we do.
We replace damaged shakes and fix the flashing around them. If the whole roof is near the end, we'll tell you, and a DaVinci or Brava roof is the way many owners keep the look without the upkeep.

sections.heading: Metal Roof Leaks
body: Metal roofs leak at the places where metal is joined or fastened: seams, penetrations, flashings and exposed screws that have backed out. A standing seam roof hides its fasteners, so a leak there usually means a seam, a flashing or a damaged panel.

Metal also moves. It grows in the summer sun and shrinks on a cold night, so a dab of sealant over a gap cracks loose within a season. Curved and odd-shaped roofs are harder still, because the flashing has to be bent to fit the shape.
We repair metal roof leaks by fixing the joint or flashing that failed, not by caulking over it.

sections.quote: I have a radius metal roof that I've had other roofers tried to fix for me and finally I found the roofer that that did the repair correctly.
sections.name: Rhonda P.

sections.heading: Shingle and Composition Roof Repair
body: Shingle roofs usually leak at the edges of things. Wind lifts and creases tabs, the rubber boot around a plumbing vent cracks in the sun, and nails back out under the shingle above.
We replace missing and damaged shingles, redo worn flashing and fix the leaks around vents and valleys. We also repair DaVinci roofs.
If hail or wind caused the damage, the repair may be covered. Jason works with your insurance company from the first call to the last nail.

items.q: Why did my roof leak after someone else fixed it?
items.a: Because the repair addressed where the water showed up, not where it got in. It's the most common reason a repair doesn't hold.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Google and your call buttons use (316) 655-9777, while your header also shows (316) 264-1511 and a Claims Pages listing gives only that one, so which number should every listing lead with?
Your banner says Roofing Since 1981, your About page says 30-plus years and your homepage says over 40, so which line should every listing use?
Your site shows no hours, while MapQuest lists Monday to Saturday, 7 am to 6 pm, so are those the hours Google and every listing should show?

onboardingQuestions: What is (316) 264-1511 for (office, sales, an old line, a crew line)? It is shown as "Office" and second after (316) 655-9777. Should it be tap-to-call?
Years in business: the site says "Roofing Since 1981" but also "30-plus years" and "over 40 years". We used "since 1981". Confirm.
Is the estimate free? We say "written estimate" only. Is there an email address for quotes?
Office hours (MapQuest lists Mon to Sat 7 am to 6 pm; the site lists none).
Financing: offered, and through whom? Nothing is claimed.
Certifications to verify before we claim any: Brava (the site says "certified installer"), DaVinci, GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, Malarkey, IKO. We claim none.
BBB: the site says "A plus"; unverified, not used.
License and registration numbers (Kansas registration, Attorney General roofing registration) and insurance. None is shown.
Warranty terms in writing: workmanship 5, 10 and 15 years (which jobs get which), and manufacturer warranties.
Subcontractors: one 1-star review says a subcontractor did a roof, while the site says no commissioned salespeople. Does the crew include subcontractors?
Flat and EPDM roofs: the commercial page lists an EPDM job and one review says flat roofs are not their expertise. Do they want flat roofs offered?
Commercial: only four project names on the site. Which commercial work do they want to promote?
Names of the two lead foremen, and Jason's title (the owner reviews call him the business manager).
Legal name "Douglas Fry Roofing, Inc.": the pages use "Douglas Fry Roofing". Which should lead?
Service area: confirm Hays and Great Bend (named on the site) and how far they will travel.
Who receives the homepage form submissions, and does it work?
The three testimonials on the old site (Amber Snavely, Tony Martinez, Steve Lebeda): where from, and may we use them?
Jason's role: the pages say he handles most inspections, estimates and insurance calls himself (from about 43 reviews). Confirm that is accurate, and whether a lead foreman ever does the inspection.

Tile track record: the pages say you have lifted and relaid clay tile roofs, reused original tile over new underlayment and ordered matching tile (from reviews by Connie P. and Linda G.), and list a barrel concrete tile project at Newman University. Confirm the Newman job was your install.
Logo file, brand colors and real job photos for the build.
